comments.author: Just-Juggernaut-5190
comments.body:
When your project is small, the model has a very clean problem: make inventory, make combat, make a save system, make this menu. It can crush those individually. Once the game gets larger, you start getting interactions between systems, weird save/load states, UI navigation issues, edge cases nobody thought about, balance problems, performance problems, bad UX, inconsistent art, things that technically work but aren’t fun, bugs caused by changes made three weeks ago, etc...

It's not impossible, far from it, but it takes longer than a handful of prompts if you want quality output.

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: How easy do you think making a game is? 2D animation isn't easier than 3D animation, it's actually harder. AI can't generate proper spritesheets, except for very low res ones, then you're gonna have to edit each sprite or rig them. And that takes a lot of time. Depending on the scope of your game the time you're gonna sink will increase exponentially. I'm making a 2D game and I've done 10x more than I could've done without AI but it's still gonna take me around a year to complete my game.
